glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Learn what the terms on the platform mean
glossary.defMcap: Total value of all coins or shares in circulation. Calculated as price × circulating supply. Used to compare the relative size of assets.
glossary.def24h: Price change over the last 24 hours, expressed as a percentage. Green usually means up, red means down.
glossary.defVolume: Total value of trades (buy + sell) in the last 24 hours. Higher volume often means more interest and liquidity.
glossary.defPrice: Current market price for one unit of the asset (e.g. one token or one share).
glossary.defLiquidity: How easily an asset can be bought or sold without moving the price. Higher liquidity usually means tighter spreads and less slippage.
glossary.defFearGreed: A sentiment index (0–100) that measures whether the market is driven by fear (caution, selling) or greed (optimism, buying). Used as a contrarian or confirmation signal.
glossary.defAltSeason: A period when alternative coins (altcoins) tend to outperform Bitcoin. The index shows how much capital is flowing into BTC vs other crypto.
glossary.defDominance: The share of total crypto market cap held by one asset (e.g. BTC dominance). Helps gauge whether money is in "safe" assets or riskier alts.
glossary.defRiskOnOff: Whether investors are favoring riskier assets (stocks, crypto) or safer ones (bonds, cash). In stocks mode this reflects allocation to growth vs defensive.
glossary.defOnChain: Data and activity that happens on the blockchain: transactions, wallet movements, smart contract calls. "On-chain" metrics are taken directly from the chain.
glossary.defFunding: A periodic payment between long and short positions in perpetual futures. Positive funding means longs pay shorts; negative means shorts pay longs.
glossary.defLiquidations: When a leveraged position is forcibly closed because collateral falls below a threshold. Large liquidations can cause sharp price moves.
glossary.defWhaleFlows: Large transfers of assets by big holders (whales). Used to spot accumulation, distribution, or potential market-moving activity.
glossary.defCommandCenter: The central panel on the landing page with tabs for Analysis, News, Flows, Mindshare, and Calendar. It aggregates market context and narratives.
glossary.defWatchlist: Your saved list of tokens or stocks. Prices and stats update in real time so you can track what you care about.
glossary.defTopCoins: A list or table of major crypto assets (or stocks in stocks mode) with price, change, volume, and market cap. Click a row to open the chart.
glossary.defPredictionMarkets: Markets where you can trade on the outcome of events (e.g. elections, sports). Prices reflect the market's implied probability.
glossary.defNarrative: How a theme (e.g. AI tokens, memes) moves from early hype to maturity or exhaustion. The Mindshare tab shows where different narratives sit on that timeline.

fearGreedPage.factorTipMomentum: Ratio of gainers to losers among top coins. High momentum (many gainers) = greed; mostly losers = fear. Measures the market's directional conviction.
fearGreedPage.factorTipVolatility: Measures the spread between top gains and top losses. Low volatility suggests calm/greed; high volatility signals panic and fear-driven selling.
fearGreedPage.factorTipVolume: Total 24h trading volume relative to total market cap. High volume/cap ratio = active participation (greed); low ratio = apathy (fear).
fearGreedPage.factorTipDominance: Bitcoin's market share, inverted. When BTC dominance is high, capital is fleeing to safety (fear). When low, money flows into altcoins (greed).
fearGreedPage.factorsSectionTip: Four key signals that drive the Fear & Greed Index. Each factor is scored 0-100 and classified as Fear, Neutral, or Greed.
fearGreedPage.metricTipTotalMarketCap: Total value of all cryptocurrencies combined. Rising market cap signals broad capital inflow; declining cap suggests risk-off sentiment.
fearGreedPage.metricTipBtcDominance: Bitcoin's share of total crypto market cap. High dominance (>50%) = flight to safety. Low dominance = altcoin season / risk appetite.
fearGreedPage.metricTipEthDominance: Ethereum's share of total crypto market cap. Rising ETH dominance often correlates with DeFi and smart-contract activity growth.
fearGreedPage.metricTipVolume24h: Total trading volume across all cryptocurrencies in the last 24 hours. High volume confirms price trends; low volume may signal weak conviction.
fearGreedPage.metricTipActiveCryptos: Number of actively traded cryptocurrencies. A growing count indicates ecosystem expansion and speculative interest.
fearGreedPage.metricTipDefiMarketCap: Total market capitalization of DeFi (Decentralized Finance) protocols. Tracks the growth of on-chain lending, trading, and yield platforms.
fearGreedPage.metricTipDefiVolume24h: 24-hour trading volume across DeFi protocols. High DeFi volume signals active on-chain participation beyond centralized exchanges.
fearGreedPage.metricTipStablecoinVolume24h: 24-hour stablecoin transfer volume. High stablecoin activity often signals capital positioning — dry powder waiting to enter or exit the market.
fearGreedPage.indexTip: The Fear & Greed Index measures overall crypto market sentiment on a 0-100 scale. 0 = Extreme Fear (investors are very worried), 100 = Extreme Greed (market is overheated). It aggregates momentum, volatility, volume, and dominance signals.
fearGreedPage.historicalValuesTip: Sentiment snapshots from 1 day, 7 days, and 30 days ago. Compare with today's reading to spot trend reversals or persistent fear/greed streaks.
fearGreedPage.distributionTip: How often the index has fallen into each 10-point bucket over its entire history. Shows whether the current reading is common or rare — a reading in a thin bucket is statistically unusual.
fearGreedPage.forwardReturnsTip: Backtested average BTC returns after the index was in each sentiment zone. Shows what happened historically 7, 30, 60, and 90 days later. Past performance does not guarantee future results.
fearGreedPage.comparisonsTip: How much the index has moved over 1 day, 7 days, and 30 days. Large swings often precede significant market moves.
fearGreedPage.reasonTip: Live market-regime classification from the Spectre data layer. Combines Fear & Greed, BTC dominance, alt-season index, and 30-day bullish-asset breadth.

howToBuy.title: Getting exposure to {{company}}
howToBuy.sub: {{company}} is private, so its shares are not on an exchange. These are the routes that exist — what each one really gets you, and what it costs you to use it.
howToBuy.backerBody: These companies invested their <1>own balance sheet</1> in {{company}}, so their shareholders hold that stake indirectly. It is the only route here with no accreditation requirement — and the most diluted: the stake is one line on a very large balance sheet, and the share price answers to everything else that company does.
howToBuy.backerWarn_one: {{names}} is also on the cap table but is <1>not</1> a route: it invested client money through funds, so buying {{tickers}} buys the fee business, not the position.
howToBuy.backerWarn_other: {{names}} are also on the cap table but are <1>not</1> a route: they invested client money through funds, so buying {{tickers}} buys the fee business, not the position.
howToBuy.secondaryBody: Employees and early investors sell existing shares here. This is direct exposure, and it is the route with the most conditions attached: US buyers must generally be accredited, minimums run into the tens of thousands, the company can refuse the transfer, and the price is whatever clears today — <1>not</1> the last round on this page. Listings for any one name come and go.
howToBuy.vehiclesTitle: Listed vehicles that hold private companies
howToBuy.vehiclesBody: These trade like a stock and hold private positions inside. Whether either holds {{company}} today is theirs to disclose — check the current holdings before assuming, and check what the vehicle trades at against its own net asset value.
howToBuy.listingFiled: {{company}} has moved toward a public listing, so the ordinary route may open on its own. A first-day price is set by the book, not by the last private round.
howToBuy.listingNotFiled: {{company}} has not filed. Nothing on this page is a schedule — an expected listing is a market expectation, not a commitment by the company.
howToBuy.disclaimer: Information, not advice, and not a recommendation to buy anything. Private shares are illiquid, can be written down, and can go to zero; secondary prices differ from the last round; venues charge fees that materially change your outcome. Verify eligibility and current terms with the venue itself.

edu.usStockMarket: The combined value of every US-listed company. It sets the tone for risk everywhere - when it rises, money is confident; when it falls, caution spreads (crypto usually follows).
edu.cryptoMarketCap: The total value of all crypto - every coin's price times how many exist. It is the size of the whole market: bigger = more money already parked in, and it moves slower than any single coin.
edu.vixIndex: The VIX is the stock market's "fear gauge" - how much investors expect prices to swing. High VIX (25+) = anxiety and big moves; low VIX (under 15) = calm and complacency.
edu.fearAndGreed: A 0-100 mood gauge for crypto. Low = fear (people selling, often near bottoms); high = greed (euphoria, often near tops). Seasoned traders use it as a contrarian compass - not a buy/sell signal on its own.
edu.indexAllocation: How the market splits across the big indices (S&P 500, Nasdaq, small caps, commodities). It shows where money is concentrated and which part of the market is leading.
edu.marketDominance: Each coin's share of the total crypto market cap. Rising Bitcoin dominance means money is favoring BTC over smaller coins (risk-off); falling dominance often signals "alt season" - capital rotating into altcoins.
edu.usMarketStatus: Whether the US stock market (NYSE/Nasdaq) is open right now. Crypto trades 24/7, but it often moves in step with stocks during US trading hours - so this tells you when the "big money" is active.
